subject: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps (batching, caching, token economics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmecorp.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps (batching, caching, token economics)

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation and a helpful view into Acme's priorities. Per our call, I wanted to capture the main pain points, the levers we discussed for cost and latency, and proposed next steps so your team can review internally.

Summary of pain points
- Rising inference spend as Acme scales (primary concern from product & finance).
- Wide variance in latency at the 95th percentile during peak periods — impacts UX for conversational flows.
- Need a predictable budget for Q1 with clear ROI case to present to finance.

Goals you shared
- Reduce per-call / per-conversation unit cost by ~30-40% while keeping 95th percentile latency under 300ms for targeted routes.
- Validate ROI within a single quarter (3 months) for the initial pilot.
- Maintain output quality for customer-facing flows (no degradation >5% on your evaluation prompt set).

Technical levers we covered (initial TCO playbook)
- Batching: configure request-level batching with adaptive latency SLOs to drive throughput improvements for high-concurrency routes.
- Prefix / KV caching: cache repeated prompts and conversation prefixes to avoid re-computing tokens for common patterns.
- Model variant & quantization: evaluate a tuned, smaller model variant with int8 quantization for non-critical routes.
- Response budgeting: truncate or lower max tokens for assistant messages that don’t require long-form responses.
- Request routing: route lower-priority traffic to lower-cost capacity (Dedicated burst / hosted fallbacks) to preserve SLAs for critical routes.

High-level TCO snapshot (ballpark)
- Baseline (your numbers): ~10M tokens/month (prompt+response), estimated current spend: ~$20,000/month.
- Expected with optimizations: effective billed tokens ~6–7M/month (30–40% reduction) -> estimated spend ~$12,000–$14,000/month.
- Potential additional cost: Dedicated reserved capacity for peak SLOs (optional) estimated at ~$4k–$6k/month depending on throughput commitments.
- Net: expected monthly savings ~25–35% vs current, payback for pilot investment in ~2–3 months assuming similar usage profile.

Next steps (recommended)
1) I’ll share the TCO workbook (attached) — please drop in your real traffic numbers or give us a sample of logs so we can firm numbers.
2) Pilot scope: 2–4 week pilot on 1–2 high-volume routes (batching + KV cache) to measure real-world token reduction and latency impact.
3) Schedule a deep-dive to review the completed workbook & pilot plan: proposed slots Fri 20 Nov 10:00–10:45 AM PT or Mon 23 Nov 9:00–9:45 AM PT.
4) Procurement: please confirm who from procurement we should include for pricing and PO discussions (we’ll prepare a preliminary MSA/PO and estimated pricing).

Attachments: acme-tco-estimate.xlsx (workbook), redwood-tco-methodology.pdf (notes on assumptions).

If useful, Rafael and I can run a short demo of the batching + cache behavior using a small subset of your traffic before the pilot. Thanks — talk soon.

Regards,
Marissa Cole

2) Caching: curious if the KV/prefix caching you recommend would materially increase latency for first requests or affect model fidelity for customer-facing flows. We can’t have accuracy regressions >5% on our key eval prompts.

3) Procurement timeline: procurement will want a 30–60 day review. Can you include a simple PO/MSA starter (even a draft estimate) so I can loop them in?

Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme TCO recap & next steps (batching, caching, token economics)

Jordan — great, thanks for the quick call confirmation. A few clarifications inline and a slightly more detailed estimate attached.

1) Per-token assumptions
- Baseline calculation used your shared traffic profile (avg 120 tokens per prompt, avg 240 tokens per response -> ~360 tokens per conversation). That maps to ~10M tokens/month given your reported request volume. We used an internal blended per-token cost of $0.002 (hosted equivalent) to model baseline spend = ~$20k/mo.

2) Caching & accuracy
- KV/prefix caching only avoids re-computation for identical prefixes — cold-start latency is unchanged for first requests. In our pilot we’ll measure any subtle accuracy changes on your eval prompt set; in practice caching does not modify model weights or logits — it only serves cached outputs where identical prefixes occur, so fidelity is preserved for cached matches. For routes with high variance we recommend combining light quantization + focused evals rather than full caching.

3) More granular estimate (attached workbook) — high level numbers here:
- Baseline: 10M billed tokens/mo -> $20,000/mo
- Optimized (batching + KV cache + response budgeting): effective billed tokens 6.5M/mo -> ~$13,000/mo
- Optional: Dedicated reserved capacity for peak SLAs: +$5,000/mo (but reduces unit cost under high sustained throughput)
- Expected net savings: ~$7k/mo (~35% reduction)
- Pilot cost: typically we run the pilot under our hosted env with shared capacity; if you'd like reserved GPU for the pilot add-on it's ~ $2k for the 2–4 week window.

4) Procurement/contract starter
- I’ve attached a simple estimate and a PoC appendix. I’ll also upload a draft MSA/PO to the DocuSign link and share with Priya so procurement has a starting doc. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-REDW-PO-2026

5) Next steps & ask 
- Please upload a 24–72 hour sample of anonymized logs (or allow us scoped read-only access) so we can run the workbook on real traffic.
- Confirm pilot routes (two suggested: customer-support-chat and in-app suggestions).
- Confirm Friday 20 Nov 10:00 AM PT — invite sent.

Attached: acme-tco-estimate.xlsx, redwood-tco-methodology.pdf

If it helps, Rafael and I can run a 20-minute technical session during the pilot to show batching behavior and cache hit diagnostics.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
